implementation_readiness.transaction: DwgBlockScopeTransaction journals source-scoped events and retires each detached lease only on successful completion events. A later replay failure can leave already delivered callback prefixes, so a callback or individual Published ledger entry alone is insufficient to establish entire block commit. readDwgBlocks reports false for replay failure, and dwgRW::processDwg calls OBJECTS only when BLOCKS returned true. Thus a carefully selected post-BLOCKS OBJECTS-phase reread avoids changing block journal/event/lease behavior; additionally require the exact source tuple and Published-once ledger entry, successful whole import, finalized complete coverage, no reader integrity transition violation, and zero object/entity parse failures before private ticket delivery. Entity sweep has a contained-failure path, so its success alone is not sufficient.
implementation_readiness.next_slice: Opt-in exact selected TABLE handle in the private candidate sink. In the AC1018 OBJECTS phase, use source ledger handle/offset/ordinal/DecodedBuffer tuple, re-read from the same decoded OBJECTS buffer with DwgObjectFrame::readAt, verify its CRC and hard limits, require reader-owned class-map identity ACAD_TABLE/AcDbTable, resolve encoded type from bytes, independently walk bounded common selector and H3 xdictionary fields, and cross-check the selected 0xbb dictionary candidate's owner and exact source tuple. Stage a reader-created non-copyable capability and deliver only after whole-import completion, then assemble privately only if every selected ticket is present and unique. Follow existing candidate budgets, clear all pending state on any failed selection, duplicate, allocation failure or read retry, and preserve ordinary callbacks and Unknown generic AC1018 evidence. No candidate or public callback alone grants output authority.
implementation_readiness.tests: Generated valid controls and physical source opt-in; mutate class tuple, self handle, EED, proxy length/bounds, entmode, reactor count, xdictionary flag, role/value, CRC, byte span and source tuple; truncate at each relevant boundary; check forged or duplicate callback/ticket, candidate subset, memory-budget failure, exception, aborted later block event, contained sweep failure, import failure and retry. Check ordinary 2D TABLE callbacks and block rollback remain identical with opt-in disabled and no candidate leaks on failure.
